raw_response:
I am already old, so I do not toss money around. My land is only 2 mu, and cotton is what I know. I have grown it many years, and I watch what the other cotton growers nearby do. If the spring looks normal, I will still plant cotton, because changing crop on such a small piece is risky and I do not know the other crops as well. Cotton needs steady care, but with 3 people in the house we can manage most of the work ourselves. I have a well, so if the sky stays dry I can give water, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times.

For seed, I will buy the kind people nearby can get easily, not something fancy and expensive. For fertilizer, I would rather put a moderate amount than too little, because if cotton grows weak later it is hard to recover. But I also cannot spend too much at once, so I will split it: some before planting, some later when the plants are growing well. I do not spray unless I see a real problem, but cotton can get insects, so I will keep one or two sprays in mind. I will do ordinary tillage before planting, nothing complicated. If the year is smooth, I think the yield can be decent, but I do not count on a very high harvest at my age and with such a small plot.
